svg.title: Visual symptoms not from the eyeball: double vision sorts by which nerve palsy (third, fourth or sixth), a gaze-evoked nystagmus points to the cerebellum or brainstem, unequal pupils sort by whether the difference is worse in light (parasympathetic) or dark (sympathetic, Horner), and a relative afferent pupillary defect points to one optic nerve; nystagmus is pendular or (mostly) jerk, and the panel below localizes each visual field defect along the visual pathway
